title: 08_new_receiver_count.va is a self-declared nonconforming acceptance snapshot: a conforming compiler rejects the call and therefore FAILS the fixture

The fixture's own first line says 'NONCONFORMING ACCEPTANCE SNAPSHOT' and COVERAGE.md sG-1 repeats it. VERIFIED third: ch9-system.html:1621 marks $receiver_count itself 'Non-normative ... Where a simulator provides it', so no value is derivable; Annex G 7793 is an informative revision row. VERIFIED fourth: the header claims 'the contribution below carries V(p,n) and not the count' but the code is `I(p,n) <+ V(p,n) + $receiver_count(p)` - the residual is pinned to the undefined value too. Do NOT re-add a numeric want for $receiver_count anywhere, even inside a connectmodule: the count depends on the elaborated netlist.

New file with `` `timescale 1ns/1ns ``, `//! time 1e-6`, `//! print none`, `//! lrm G.1`, `//! lrm 9.10`, and `//! xfail VerA aliases $realtime to $abstime (codegen.zig:2528) and ignores `timescale (preprocessor.zig:91), so $realtime reads seconds instead of timescale units`.

Derivation: t = 1e-6 s / 1e-9 s per unit = 1000 exactly; both operands exactly representable, so CHECKX not CHECKR. A second point with `timescale 1us/1us giving $realtime = 1.0 would pin the scaling itself, but one file is enough to kill the alias.

title: Of G.2.2's three surviving null positions, only the conditional is tested - the analog case arm is untested
detail: VERIFIED. annex-g-changes.html:320 names exactly three survivors: 'case, conditionals and the event statement'. 05 covers the conditional. `grep -rnE ':[[:space:]]*;' --include='*.va'` over 859 files returns ONE hit, annex_a_syntax/15_case_generate.va, and that is a `generate case` default arm at module level (6.6.2), not an `analog_case_item ::= analog_expression {, analog_expression} : analog_statement_or_null` (annex-a-syntax.html:811). The discriminating risk is arm binding: a parser that treats the `;` as absent makes the NEXT arm's statement the body of the matched arm. VERIFIED against the compiler: the construct is accepted today, so this fixture is green on arrival - it is pure coverage, not a bug report.
expected: Must COMPILE and RUN. `//! lrm G.2.2`, `//! lrm A.6.6`. Body: `parameter integer mode = 1; real y; analog begin y = 2.0; case (mode) 0: y = 3.0; 1: ; default: y = 9.0; endcase ... end` with `CHECKX("the null case arm matched and did nothing", y, 2.0)`. Derivation: y is 2.0 before the case, mode = 1 selects the null arm, nothing executes. Every mis-parse gives a different number: a skipped `;` makes `y = 9.0` the body of arm 1 (9.0), fall-through gives 9.0, matching arm 0 gives 3.0.

section: G.1 Table G.7 item 7922 ('Remove error for contributing to a port declared with an input direction. This is now a warning', 5.6.1)
title: The 2023 relaxation is exercised but never PROVEN: the one fixture that contributes to an input port force-biases the node, so a dropped contribution is invisible
detail: PARTIALLY VERIFIED - the uncovered lens overstated this. Its claim 'No fixture contributes to an input port' is FALSE: tests/fixtures/ch06_hierarchy/input_port.va declares `module ch6_input(input electrical p)` and does `I(p) <+ V(p);`, so it compiles and runs today, and the negatives lens was right that no reject fixture exists and that none may be added. What survives is weaker but real: input_port.va carries `//! bias V(p) = 1.25` and asserts only `V(p) == 1.25`, i.e. it checks the BIAS, not the effect of the contribution - a compiler that parsed and then silently discarded the contribution to an input port passes it unchanged. Downgraded from the lens's medium to low for that reason. 5.6.1 now reads 'Implementations may issue a warning' - MAY, so the module must still compile and run. VERIFIED against the compiler: an unbiased input-port contribution is accepted, so this is green on arrival.
expected: Must COMPILE and RUN. `//! lrm G.1`, `//! lrm 5.6.1`, and NO `//! bias` on the input node so the solve determines it. Body: `module m(i, p); input i; inout p; electrical i, p; analog begin I(i) <+ V(i)*1.0e-3 - 1.0e-3; I(p) <+ V(p); ... end`. `CHECKX("the contribution to the input port was honoured, not dropped", V(i), 1.0);` Derivation: the only branch at i is the contributed flow, KCL makes it zero, so V(i)*1e-3 = 1e-3 and V(i) = 1.0 exactly (a 1 kohm conductance driven by 1 mA). The number separates all three wrong behaviours: an error (does not compile), a dropped contribution (0.0) and probe-only (0.0). Do NOT add a reject fixture for this rule anywhere - the prohibition was deleted in 2023.

title: Three legacy .expected-error.txt sidecars are a second oracle the README abolished
detail: VERIFIED: all three exist, and README.md opens with 'No sidecar files' / 'there is no second file to drift out of step with it'. They are the old tests/conformance.zig oracle. Today they agree with their `.va` headers; nothing keeps them agreeing, and none can carry a `//! lrm` cite - so every expectation strengthened by G-10/G-11/G-12 stops being reflected in its sidecar the moment it lands. SCOPE CORRECTION to both lenses: 301 such sidecars exist across the whole suite, so this is a suite-wide migration, not an annex_g defect. Deleting the three in this chapter is correct and costs nothing, but do not treat it as closing the contract violation.
expected: Delete all three files after G-10, G-11 and G-12 land. The substrings they carry (E0205/forever, expression/generate, ParseError) are superseded by the corrected `//! reject` lines in the `.va` files - note 04's sidecar and 06's sidecar are both WEAKER than what G-10/G-11 install, which is the drift argument made concrete.
